decision.title: PARTIAL ROOT CAUSE
decision.outcome: CONTINUE — run a bounded real-scene follow-up before changing the shared output core or promoting the Anatomy candidate.
decision.confidence: High for the controlled output-stage finding; insufficient to explain the real Anatomy candidate's large state-dependent errors.
decision.summary: The controlled fixture shows that output-transform staging changes RGB results while preserving alpha. The material-aware path matches WebGL within one RGB code value on this fixture, but the same candidate remains worse than standard WebGPU in most high-priority real Anatomy states. No complete real-scene root cause is isolated.

provenance.hardwareAccelerationEvidence: No independent browser/system GPU diagnostics were collected.

findings: NodeMaterial.setupDiffuseColor multiplies diffuse alpha by material opacity; opaque materials force alpha to 1.
ToneMappingNode transforms RGB and passes input alpha through unchanged; ColorSpaceNode conversions also preserve alpha.
NodeMaterial.setupOutput itself applies fog and optional premultiplication; it does not add renderer tone mapping or output color-space conversion.
The WebGL shader applies the selected per-material tone mapping and output color-space conversion before the fragment reaches fixed-function blending.

For the on-screen WebGPU output path, transparent objects render into the common working-color-space framebuffer target; Renderer._renderOutput then runs a completed-image RenderOutputNode that clamps alpha, unpremultiplies, tone maps, converts color space, and premultiplies.
The material-aware adapter moves the per-material tone-mapping and sRGB conversion into each adapted NodeMaterial.setupOutput hook before blending. Its conversions are RGB-only and retain alpha.
Three.js common and WebGL render lists both include groupOrder, renderOrder, and depth in their transparent sorting keys; the fixture also recorded matching actual draw callbacks.

clearCanvasAlpha.lineNote: Line sample alpha includes raster coverage and is compared across modes rather than required to equal source opacity.

controlledFixture.interpretation: RGB changes are reported separately from measured framebuffer alpha. The measured channel data does not use a guessed sRGB blend equation; the source trace and matched captures establish the tested pipeline-stage distinction.

webgpuMaterialAware.adapterProbeInterpretation: timed-out is unknown diagnostic evidence; mounted renderer identity/backend is authoritative

aggregateMeasurements.methodology: Equal-weight mean across projected object-aligned ROI MAEs. Regions can overlap, so ROI count is not a count of unique independent framebuffer pixels; values are descriptive and are not a parity threshold.

exactBackgroundAndGroundGlassComparisons.interpretation: The top-left canvas-background reference sample is distinct from object pixels. The standard WebGPU capture differs from WebGL in this patch; material-aware WebGPU matches WebGL. Existing object-aligned ROIs are rectangular and not background-masked, so empty pixels inside those rectangles may contribute; that contribution was not separately quantified. Exact Ground Glass comparison is across all 13 states and all three mode pairs.

sceneInputParity.normalization: Per-run object/material/geometry UUIDs and candidate-only adapted flags are excluded; renderable names, roles, transforms, state flags, geometry type/count/version and source material property values remain compared.
sceneInputParity.projectionNote: WebGPU and WebGL use different normalized depth projection terms; camera position/quaternion, target, horizontal/vertical projection terms and displayed scene view are matched.

hypotheses.classification: rejected as the cause of the tested RGB discrepancy
hypotheses.result: Across 288 matched clear-canvas RGBA sample comparisons, cross-mode alpha difference was zero; Basic and Standard material alpha tracked source opacity within the asserted two-code-value bound.
hypotheses.confidence: High for the tested fixture/material families; not every renderer compositor.

hypotheses.classification: confirmed contributing factor in the controlled fixture; not a complete Anatomy root cause
hypotheses.result: Standard WebGPU RGB differed from WebGL for Basic, Standard, and Line fixtures. The material-aware per-material output path reduced the measured error to <=1 RGB code value. This supports output-transform staging/per-material tone-mapping treatment as a controlled discrepancy category, but does not explain why the real Anatomy candidate remains worse overall.
hypotheses.confidence: High for the controlled output-stage contribution; low for explaining real Anatomy states.

hypotheses.result: Toggling premultipliedAlpha caused zero measured center-pixel change in WebGL and material-aware WebGPU in the tested one/two-layer compositions.
hypotheses.confidence: Medium; only tested normal-blending center-pixel cases.

hypotheses.classification: rejected as the cause of the cross-backend mismatch in tested depth cases
hypotheses.result: Depth-write changes materially affected the reference sample, but material-aware WebGPU matched WebGL within RGB MAE 1 across all tested depth cases.
hypotheses.confidence: High for tested depth controls; not all scene intersections.

hypotheses.classification: rejected as the cause of the cross-backend mismatch in tested sort cases
hypotheses.result: Adding layers and explicit render-order swaps changed measured pixels and actual draw callbacks; draw order matched across modes and material-aware pixels stayed within RGB MAE 1 of WebGL.

hypotheses.classification: rejected for the tested dynamic property propagation path
hypotheses.result: The tracker propagated source material changes into stable adapted outputs; a replacement source produced a new output. Real candidate source/output values also matched for all 15 tested fields across the collected assignments.
hypotheses.confidence: High for the captured properties and replacement stages.

hypotheses.classification: rejected for the tested shader-state transitions
hypotheses.result: Transparency and tone-mapping signature changes advanced adapted output versions as expected and captured candidate pixels tracked WebGL across stages.
hypotheses.confidence: High for tested transparency/tone-mapping shader-state transitions.

hypotheses.classification: rejected as a mismatched camera view or source-material/geometry input for the 13 measured states
hypotheses.result: Position, quaternion, orbit target and x/y projection terms match across all 13 states; 26 normalized renderable-pair comparisons and 1,256 source-material assignment comparisons have no mismatch. WebGPU depth projection terms differ by renderer coordinate convention. The evidence does not isolate the real-scene cause of the remaining pixel differences.
hypotheses.confidence: High for the recorded camera pose, geometry, transform, and source-property comparisons; does not identify the pixel cause.

hypotheses.classification: same-mode noise rejected; background and rectangular-ROI contributions remain unquantified
hypotheses.result: Repeat noise is zero in the controlled fixture and real audit. The sampled top-left canvas-background patch differs by RGB MAE 24.67 between WebGL and standard WebGPU but is exact between WebGL and the material-aware candidate. Object-aligned rectangles are not foreground masked, so empty-area contribution remains unknown; it cannot alone explain the candidate-specific subject differences.
hypotheses.confidence: High that repeats were stable and the sampled background differs; low for foreground-only ROI attribution.

recommendation.nextDecision: Do not implement a full Anatomy output correction from this evidence alone.
recommendation.nextInvestigation: Isolate the real scene's material-family and overlap combinations using per-renderable/material contribution captures or a narrowly scoped state-by-state negative control, then test the predicted output-stage correction against the actual high-error Anatomy ROIs.
recommendation.likelyCorrectionSurfaceIfConfirmed: The shared material-aware NodeMaterial.setupOutput output adapter, kept opt-in and covered by the controlled alpha/RGB fixture.
requiredRegressionGates: The controlled per-family opaque/transparent matrix must preserve measured alpha and keep candidate output within the measured WebGL fixture envelope.
Retain the 13 matched Anatomy states and meaningful object-specific ROIs without relaxing thresholds.
Run Architecture Rise's existing strict native parity gate before changing the shared output core.
Verify module-shared Anatomy source resources and independent WebGL Ground Glass.
Verify production remains WebGL-only and Anatomy remains explicit-only until independent parity acceptance.
recommendation.architectureRiseRisk: The same output adapter is shared with Architecture Rise; any output-stage change must rerun its 81-criterion contract.
recommendation.groundGlassRisk: No Ground Glass code changed; the measured RTT remains independently WebGL2 and contentful.
recommendation.ownershipRisk: No resource tracker, source ownership, or disposal behavior changed; probe additions are observation-only.

diagnosticChanges: The isolated benchmark fixture owns its own renderer, scene, and disposable resources; it is imported only by its standalone test HTML.
The Anatomy audit probe now records source/output properties, renderable transforms, geometry attribute versions, and output material references for evidence only.
The audit accepts an adapter probe timeout as unknown while still requiring the actual mounted WebGPU renderer/backend, one initialization attempt, no failure, and no application fallback.

limitations: Chrome 155 on macOS arm64 exposed a native WebGPU adapter, but no independent browser/system GPU diagnostics were collected; hardware acceleration is unconfirmed.

The real Anatomy audit's separate bounded adapter probe returned timed-out during the captured mount. The actual renderer, execution backend, initialization count, output readiness, and no-fallback assertions passed; timed-out is not treated as adapter success.
The controlled fixture does not include the actual Anatomy world environment, shadow composition, and full transparent geometry stack; it isolates rather than reproduces that scene.
No GPU timing or hardware performance claim is made. Frame cadence is not GPU execution time.
No cross-backend parity threshold was approved by this investigation; reported MAE values are descriptive.
